title: Release validation
text:
A release fingerprint hashes sorted relative paths, sizes, and file contents. Source and staging accept ordinary local files only. Fresh clones additionally permit git-annex links into their own object store. Frictionless checks both metadata and resource contents; schemas must be inline.
Resource validation uses Frictionless’s built-in multiprocessing by default, including during fresh-retrieval verification. Packages with foreign keys use sequential validation to preserve cross-resource checks. Library callers can also request validate_package(..., parallel=False).
The process pool uses Python’s available CPU count. Set PYTHON_CPU_COUNT before starting Python to limit workers, for example PYTHON_CPU_COUNT=4 uv run depot validate ID VERSION. The Slurm examples set this from SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK. Allow memory for a decoded table and pandas representation in each worker. Frictionless 5.21 does not forward custom checklists to parallel workers, so parallel validation reports its phase and elapsed time; sequential validation additionally reports individual resources and rows.

title: Release validation
DataLad publication
text:
Each dataset has one managed DataLad repository containing releases/VERSION and a local RIA archive at TARGET_ROOT/ID. DataLad configures a Git sibling plus an annex storage sibling. A RIA archive is a bare repository, so unlocking files in the publisher’s workspace cannot make ordinary files appear in Goldmine. See DataLad’s RIA layout.
The default access = "unlocked" also exposes an independent ordinary-file view at TARGET_ROOT/ID.data/releases/VERSION. After retrieval and validation, Depot copies the verified bytes there atomically and checks their fingerprint. The files are populated, writable by their owner, and contain no annex symlinks or placeholders. Group access follows filesystem permissions and the installation’s umask. There is one extra full copy of the data; no hardlinks can let user edits alter archived objects. Personal analysis copies keep the shared view intact.
Set target access = "locked" in TOML, or override with destination.access in a dataset’s registry YAML, to retain archive-only publication. New annex files in the managed workspace follow that access setting through the supported annex.addunlocked option. A fresh consumer clone still requires datalad get, regardless of pointer mode.
Repeat pushes reconcile missing views from staged bytes matching the previously verified fingerprint, retaining the original archived commit without another Frictionless pass. Changed ordinary files cause an access_conflict; they are never overwritten. A failed first materialization leaves no successful receipt and can be retried. Previous successful archive receipts remain intact. Switching to locked mode skips materialization; it does not delete an existing ordinary copy or retroactively lock earlier commits. No parent dataset is assumed.

"""DataLad CLI publication to local RIA stores, with fresh-clone verification."""

from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from .config import Config, access_mode, contained
from .errors import DepotError
from .progress import ProgressCallback, ProgressUpdate, quiet
from .validation import fingerprint, validate_package


def command(args: list[str], cwd: Path | None = None) -> str:
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return result.stdout.strip()
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise DepotError(
            "missing_tool", f"Install {args[0]} and make it available on PATH."
        ) from exc
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as exc:
        # Raw stdout/stderr can contain credentials, remote URLs, and private paths.
        raise DepotError(
            "command_failed",
            f"{args[0]} command failed; check tools, target access, and permissions.",
            {"operation": args[1], "exit_code": exc.returncode},
        ) from exc


def materialize(
    config: Config,
    manifest: dict,
    version: str,
    verified: Path,
    expected: str,
    *,
    on_progress: ProgressCallback = quiet,
) -> dict:
    """Expose verified bytes as independent ordinary files; never overwrite edits."""
    mode = access_mode(config, manifest)
    if mode == "locked":
        return {"mode": mode, "populated": False}
    target = config.targets[manifest["destination"]["target"]]
    relative = Path(manifest["id"] + ".data") / "releases" / version
    destination = target.root / relative
    # Reject redirected views even when a symlink stays within the target root.
    for path in (destination, *destination.parents):
        if path == target.root:
            break
        if path.is_symlink():
            raise DepotError(
                "unsafe_path", "The ordinary-file view cannot contain directory symlinks."
            )
    destination = contained(destination, target.root)
    on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Preparing populated, unlocked Goldmine files"))
    if destination.exists():
        if fingerprint(destination, on_progress=on_progress) != expected:
            raise DepotError(
                "access_conflict",
                "Goldmine ordinary files have changed; preserve edits and restore or relocate the view before retrying.",
            )
    else:
        destination.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".populate-", dir=destination.parent) as temporary:
            incoming = Path(temporary) / "release"
            # Follow only the annex links already checked by retrieval verification.
            # copyfile creates independent bytes, without inheriting annex read-only modes.
            shutil.copytree(verified, incoming, copy_function=shutil.copyfile)
            if fingerprint(incoming, on_progress=on_progress) != expected:
                raise DepotError(
                    "verification_failed", "Populated files differ from verified content."
                )
            incoming.replace(destination)
    for path in destination.rglob("*"):
        if path.is_file():
            path.chmod(path.stat().st_mode | 0o200)
    return {
        "mode": mode,
        "populated": True,
        "path": str(destination),
        "relative_path": relative.as_posix(),
    }


def publish(
    config: Config,
    manifest: dict,
    version: str,
    staged: Path,
    expected: str,
    on_saved: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
    on_progress: ProgressCallback = quiet,
) -> dict:
    on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Preparing DataLad publication workspace"))
    dataset_id = manifest["id"]
    dataset = config.dataset_path(config.workspace, dataset_id)
    target = config.targets[manifest["destination"]["target"]]
    store = contained(target.root / dataset_id, target.root)
    store_url = "ria+" + store.as_uri()
    clone_url = store_url + "#~" + dataset_id
    config.workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not (dataset / ".datalad/config").is_file():
        command(["datalad", "create", "-d", str(dataset), "-D", f"Depot dataset {dataset_id}"])
    command(
        [
            "git",
            "config",
            "annex.addunlocked",
            str(access_mode(config, manifest) == "unlocked").lower(),
        ],
        cwd=dataset,
    )
    destination = contained(dataset / "releases" / version, dataset)
    if destination.exists():
        # On retry the saved worktree may contain annex symlinks.
        if (
            fingerprint(destination, dataset / ".git/annex/objects", on_progress=on_progress)
            != expected
        ):
            raise DepotError(
                "version_conflict", "Managed workspace content conflicts with this version."
            )
    else:
        destination.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        # A failed copy must not strand a partial version under its final name.
        with TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".intake-", dir=dataset) as temporary:
            incoming = Path(temporary) / "release"
            on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Copying validated release into DataLad workspace"))
            shutil.copytree(staged, incoming)
            if fingerprint(incoming, on_progress=on_progress) != expected:
                raise DepotError("source_changed", "Staged content changed during publication.")
            incoming.replace(destination)
    on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Saving release with DataLad"))
    command(
        [
            "datalad",
            "save",
            "-d",
            str(dataset),
            "-m",
            f"Depot release {version}",
            str(destination),
        ],
        cwd=dataset,
    )
    # Store the release's own commit, rather than a later dataset HEAD on retry.
    commit = command(["git", "log", "-1", "--format=%H", "--", f"releases/{version}"], cwd=dataset)
    if not commit:
        raise DepotError("invalid_state", "No DataLad commit exists for the release.")
    if on_saved:
        on_saved(commit)
    configured = command(["git", "remote"], cwd=dataset).splitlines()
    if "goldmine" not in configured:
        on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Creating publication storage sibling"))
        target.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        command(
            [
                "datalad",
                "create-sibling-ria",
                "-d",
                str(dataset),
                "-s",
                "goldmine",
                "--alias",
                dataset_id,
                "--new-store-ok",
                store_url,
            ],
            cwd=dataset,
        )
    else:
        remote = command(["git", "remote", "get-url", "goldmine"], cwd=dataset)
        if not Path(remote).resolve().is_relative_to(store):
            raise DepotError(
                "target_conflict", "Existing sibling belongs to a different publication target."
            )
    on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Pushing release to publication storage"))
    command(
        ["datalad", "push", "-d", str(dataset), "--to", "goldmine", "--data", "anything"],
        cwd=dataset,
    )
    with TemporaryDirectory(prefix="verify-", dir=config.staging) as temporary:
        on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Cloning published dataset for retrieval verification"))
        clone = Path(temporary) / "clone"
        command(["datalad", "clone", clone_url, str(clone)])
        command(["git", "checkout", "--detach", commit], cwd=clone)
        # Explicitly choose the RIA storage sibling: publisher-local content cannot
        # accidentally satisfy the verification boundary.
        on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Retrieving published release from storage"))
        command(
            [
                "datalad",
                "get",
                "-d",
                str(clone),
                "--source",
                "goldmine-storage",
                str(clone / "releases" / version),
            ],
            cwd=clone,
        )
        retrieved = clone / "releases" / version
        on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Verifying retrieved release fingerprint"))
        if (
            fingerprint(retrieved, clone / ".git/annex/objects", on_progress=on_progress)
            != expected
        ):
            raise DepotError(
                "verification_failed", "Fresh retrieval does not match the validated content."
            )
        on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Validating retrieved release"))
        validate_package(
            retrieved, manifest["checks"], clone / ".git/annex/objects", on_progress=on_progress
        )
        access = materialize(
            config, manifest, version, retrieved, expected, on_progress=on_progress
        )
    on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Publication and fresh retrieval verified"))
    return {
        "commit": commit,
        "target": str(store),
        "clone_url": clone_url,
        "verified": True,
        "access": access,
    }

title: Release lifecycle and synchronization
text:
Validation evidence binds the release fingerprint to its reviewed manifest and configured target. Per-dataset locks protect state changes. Each attempt leaves a receipt; only verified publication receives success status. Repeated pushes reuse successful receipts, and sync isolates dataset failures.
The manual sequence is fetch → validate → push → catalog build → quarto render; validation requires an existing fetched candidate. Keep the same configuration for all Depot commands. sync visits all registered datasets, so use the README selected-release walkthrough for one dataset.

title: Depot operator manual
text: Depot consumes completed Prospector releases, publishes validated versions through DataLad, and generates a Quarto catalogue from verified publication receipts. Start with the README walkthrough for setup, registration, and the complete real-data workflow. This manual documents the implementation; its code blocks emit the Python modules and do not execute ingestion.

title: Depot operator manual
text:
Quickstart
Complete software and configuration setup first. The Prospector must already provide VERSION/datapackage.json and local resources; the selected registry must contain a reviewed entry for the dataset. Keep the same configuration for every step. For Kiribati, run from the Depot checkout:
export DEPOT_CONFIG="$PWD/depot.toml"
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" fetch kiribati-biomarkers v0.2.2
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" validate kiribati-biomarkers v0.2.2
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" push kiribati-biomarkers v0.2.2
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" catalog build
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring
Point the configuration’s website setting to this checkout’s notebooks/ directory; substitute another dataset ID and version as needed. Fetch must succeed before validate; validate must succeed before push. Expect fetched, validated, success, and catalogued in that order. Push records success only after a fresh clone retrieves and validates the published bytes. Inspect failures with uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" receipts kiribati-biomarkers.
The catalogue and Manual share notebooks/_quarto.yml and one output directory, docs/. Open docs/index.html to browse datasets and docs/overview.html for operating instructions. catalog build updates the landing page and generated dataset pages without changing authored Manual chapters.
For subsequent runs, uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" sync performs fetch, validate, push, and catalogue generation for every registered dataset and discovered version. It has no dataset selector. Use the individual commands to test a small dataset while another dataset is running. Render the unified site afterward. If publication is already verified, start at catalog build; see the catalogue guide.

"""Structured errors safe to display without subprocess output or credentials."""


class DepotError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: str, message: str, details: dict | None = None):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code
        self.details = details or {}

    def as_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {"code": self.code, "message": str(self), "details": self.details}

Progress callbacks report work without coupling the lifecycle to a terminal. Only the CLI renders these events with Rich; library callers remain silent by default.

"""Progress events shared by the lifecycle and its user interfaces."""

from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProgressUpdate:
    message: str
    completed: int | None = None
    total: int | None = None
    unit: str = ""


ProgressCallback = Callable[[ProgressUpdate], None]


def quiet(update: ProgressUpdate) -> None:
    """Leave library calls silent unless a caller supplies a progress callback."""

"""Atomic local records and nonblocking Linux per-dataset locks."""

from contextlib import contextmanager
import fcntl
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import NamedTemporaryFile

from .errors import DepotError


def read_json(path: Path) -> dict | None:
    try:
        return json.loads(path.read_text())
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise DepotError(
            "invalid_state", "An operational record is unreadable; inspect internal state."
        ) from exc


def write_json(path: Path, value: dict) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", dir=path.parent, delete=False) as stream:
        temporary = Path(stream.name)
        try:
            json.dump(value, stream, sort_keys=True, indent=2)
            stream.write("\n")
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        except BaseException:
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise
    try:
        temporary.replace(path)
    finally:
        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)


@contextmanager
def dataset_lock(path: Path):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("a") as stream:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(stream, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError as exc:
            raise DepotError(
                "dataset_locked", "Another operation holds this dataset's lock; retry later."
            ) from exc
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(stream, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

title: Registry and operational roots
text:
Keep operational roots outside the website. Registry manifests contain standing publication policies. Destination layers and target names must agree with the independently configured allow-list. Refined policies require explicit UTC release dates.
For the operator workflow, start with README setup, then register and publish a dataset. Configuration paths resolve from the TOML file’s directory; relative source.releases paths resolve from the registry directory. Keep the website separate from source and operational roots. Set website = "notebooks" so catalogue pages join the Manual’s existing Quarto project and both render to docs/. Private operational roots stay outside that public source tree; the configuration and publication receipts are never staged for site rendering.
Each target accepts access = "unlocked" (the default) or access = "locked". The default adds populated ordinary files at TARGET_ROOT/ID.data/releases/VERSION alongside the RIA archive. Set destination.access in a registry entry to override its target’s default for that dataset. Access settings do not change the content validation binding: switching access does not require repeating scientific checks. Locked mode skips that extra view and leaves retrieval to DataLad; it does not remove an existing view. See publication for storage and retry semantics.

Build the data catalogue
text: Catalogue entries come from data already recorded by Depot. Add or update a reviewed registry manifest and publish a release; there is no separate list of entries to maintain in Python.

title: Build the data catalogue
text:
Quickstart
Complete the README setup and registration walkthrough first. A registry entry alone does not add a catalogue row: the release must pass fetch → validate → push using the same installation configuration. If no release has been published yet, follow the real-data workflow before running the commands below.
After a successful verified push, run from the Depot checkout:
export DEPOT_CONFIG="$PWD/depot.toml"
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" catalog build
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring
Use the reviewed configuration with website = "notebooks". The existing notebooks/_quarto.yml combines the data catalogue and Operator Manual in one Quarto project. Open docs/index.html to browse datasets; use its navbar to open the Operator Manual at docs/overview.html. No second Quarto project is needed.
catalog build reads registry metadata and verified receipts into a pandas DataFrame, builds Great Tables, and writes index.qmd and datasets/ID.qmd under website. Quarto renders those pages. Follow a dataset link to see its resource table and retrieval instructions. Both steps can be repeated without publishing again; there is no Python list of entries to edit.
For routine updates across all registered datasets, use uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" sync, then run the same render helper. Sync performs fetch, validation, publication, retrieval verification, and catalogue generation. To process a selected release, use the operator quickstart.
An empty catalogue means there are no visible entries with eligible verified receipts for their configured destinations. Check publication success, catalogue.visible, the selected configuration, and the destination.

Catalogue columns and resource summaries
Great Tables for the index and dataset pages

Rendered Great Tables and page text
index.qmd and datasets/ID.qmd



Registry fields supply the title, description, visibility, and audience. Receipts supply the verified layer, version, publication time, commit, provenance, and resource summaries. Failed or unverified attempts cannot add a row; a later failed release leaves the previous verified release listed. Private paths and operational errors are excluded by the public column projection.
For exploration, use the same DataFrame and table functions as the build:
from pathlib import Path

from depot.catalog import catalogue_data, catalogue_table
from depot.config import Config

config = Config.load(Path("/path/to/depot.toml"))
entries = catalogue_data(config)
entries.loc[:, ["id", "title", "version", "published"]]
catalogue_table(entries)
The final expression displays a Great Tables table in a notebook. catalogue_table() selects and labels columns; the library constructs the table markup. Resource tables are built directly from the resource records in each receipt. Fixed table IDs keep repeated builds reproducible.
Dataset metadata and resource records are ordinary pandas DataFrames rendered with Great Tables, just like the catalogue index. Python writes the rendered tables and minimal retrieval instructions into Quarto pages; there are no page template files or template engine. Change CATALOGUE_LABELS to select displayed catalogue columns and registry YAML to update dataset descriptions. Metadata remains literal text in the tables. Great Tables’ HTML is placed in Quarto raw HTML blocks so Markdown-like cell values are not interpreted as page markup.

title: Build the data catalogue
text:
Implementation
This manual emits catalog.py; edit the block below and explicitly re-emit it. The selection policy is kept separate from DataFrame preparation and presentation. Ordinary website rendering does not execute these examples.






Tip Procedure



"""Public catalogue data frames and Great Tables, built from verified receipts."""

from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

from great_tables import GT
import pandas as pd

from .config import Config, load_manifest
from .errors import DepotError
from .service import Depot, version_key
from .storage import dataset_lock, read_json, write_json

NOTICE = "Prospects can change between versions. Refined releases follow a stricter schedule."

# An explicit projection prevents internal receipt fields from reaching the website.
PUBLIC_COLUMNS = {
    "id": "id",
    "title": "title",
    "description": "description",
    "layer": "layer",
    "audience": "audience",
    "receipt.version": "version",
    "receipt.timestamp": "published",
    "receipt.commit": "commit",
    "receipt.display.prospector": "prospector",
    "receipt.display.package_name": "package_name",
    "receipt.display.resources": "resources",
    "receipt.access.mode": "access_mode",
    "receipt.access.populated": "populated",
}
CATALOGUE_LABELS = {
    "id": "Dataset",
    "title": "Title",
    "layer": "Layer",
    "version": "Latest verified version",
    "description": "Description",
    "published": "Last published",
}


def text(value: object) -> str:
    # Quarto shortcodes use braces; encode them as well as HTML metacharacters.
    return escape(str(value), quote=True).replace("{", "{").replace("}", "}")


def public_entries(config: Config) -> list[dict]:
    depot = Depot(config)
    entries = []
    for path in sorted(config.registry.glob("*.yaml")):
        try:
            manifest = load_manifest(config, path.stem)
        except DepotError:
            # A broken current policy cannot authorize public visibility.
            continue
        if not manifest["catalogue"]["visible"]:
            continue
        target = str(config.targets[manifest["destination"]["target"]].root / manifest["id"])
        successes = [
            r
            for r in depot.receipts(manifest["id"])
            if r.get("status") == "success"
            and r.get("verified") is True
            and r.get("validation", {}).get("valid") is True
            and r.get("target") == target
        ]
        if not successes:
            continue
        receipt = max(successes, key=lambda r: (version_key(r["version"]), r["timestamp"]))
        entries.append(
            {
                "id": manifest["id"],
                "title": manifest["title"],
                "description": manifest["description"],
                "layer": receipt["display"]["layer"],
                "audience": manifest["catalogue"]["audience"],
                "receipt": receipt,
            }
        )
    return entries


def catalogue_data(config: Config) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load one public row per dataset; retain a stable schema when there are none."""
    return (
        pd.json_normalize(public_entries(config))
        .reindex(columns=list(PUBLIC_COLUMNS))
        .rename(columns=PUBLIC_COLUMNS)
        .assign(published=lambda df: df["published"].astype("string").str.split("T").str[0])
        .sort_values("id", ignore_index=True)
    )


def catalogue_table(data: pd.DataFrame) -> GT:
    """Describe the display declaratively; Great Tables owns the HTML markup."""
    return (
        GT(data.loc[:, list(CATALOGUE_LABELS)], id="depot-catalogue")
        .cols_label(**CATALOGUE_LABELS)
        .fmt(columns=list(CATALOGUE_LABELS), fns=text)
        .fmt(columns="id", fns=lambda value: f'<a href="datasets/{value}.html">{text(value)}</a>')
        .cols_align(align="left")
        .tab_options(table_width="100%")
    )


def resources_table(resources: list[dict], dataset_id: str) -> GT:
    data = pd.DataFrame.from_records(resources, columns=["name", "files", "bytes"])
    return (
        GT(data, id=f"depot-resources-{dataset_id}")
        .cols_label(name="Resource", files="Files", bytes="Bytes")
        .fmt(columns="name", fns=text)
        .fmt_integer(columns=["files", "bytes"])
        .tab_options(table_width="100%")
    )


def _write(path: Path, content: str) -> None:
    from tempfile import NamedTemporaryFile

    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", dir=path.parent, delete=False) as stream:
        stream.write(content)
        temporary = Path(stream.name)
    temporary.replace(path)


def build(config: Config) -> list[dict]:
    with dataset_lock(config.state / "catalogue.lock"):
        data = catalogue_data(config)
        pages = []
        for row in data.to_dict(orient="records"):
            dataset_id = row["id"]
            version = row["version"]
            # Operators supply the private store; the receipt pins the public commit.
            store_variable = "${DEPOT_STORE}"
            commands = (
                f'datalad clone "ria+file://{store_variable}#~{dataset_id}" {dataset_id}\n'
                f"cd {dataset_id}\n"
                f"git checkout --detach {row['commit']}\n"
                f"datalad get releases/{version}"
            )
            direct_access = ""
            if row.get("access_mode") == "unlocked" and row.get("populated") is True:
                relative = f"{row['layer']}/{dataset_id}.data/releases/{version}/"
                direct_access = (
                    "## Use the data directly\n\n"
                    "The lab's Goldmine contains populated, ordinary writable files at "
                    f"`{relative}` relative to its root. Open these files with Python, R, "
                    "or your usual tools; no DataLad commands are required. "
                    "Ask the lab operator for the Goldmine root if needed. "
                    "Work on a personal copy when making changes to a shared release.\n\n"
                )
            details = pd.DataFrame(
                {"Field": label, "Value": row[field]}
                for field, label in {
                    "id": "Dataset",
                    "title": "Title",
                    "description": "Description",
                    "layer": "Layer",
                    "version": "Version",
                    "published": "Published",
                    "commit": "Commit",
                    "prospector": "Prospector",
                    "package_name": "Package",
                    "audience": "Intended audience/use",
                }.items()
            )
            metadata_table = GT(details, id=f"depot-metadata-{dataset_id}").fmt(
                columns="Value", fns=text
            )
            page = (
                '---\ntitle: "Dataset details"\nsidebar: false\n---\n\n```{=html}\n'
                + metadata_table.as_raw_html()
                + "\n```\n\nStatus: validated, published, and verified by fresh retrieval.\n\n"
                + "## Resources\n\n```{=html}\n"
                + resources_table(row["resources"], dataset_id).as_raw_html()
                + "\n```\n\n"
                + direct_access
                + "## Retrieve the archived version with DataLad\n\n"
                + "Set `DEPOT_STORE` to the dataset's RIA store path supplied by the lab operator. "
                + "Use these commands to retrieve the pinned release:\n\n"
                + f"<pre><code>{text(commands)}</code></pre>\n\n"
                + f"Package metadata: releases/{version}/datapackage.json.\n\n{NOTICE}\n"
            )
            relative = f"datasets/{dataset_id}.qmd"
            _write(config.website / relative, page)
            pages.append(relative)
        table = (
            "```{=html}\n" + catalogue_table(data).as_raw_html() + "\n```"
            if not data.empty
            else "No verified datasets are available yet."
        )
        index = (
            '---\ntitle: "Depot data catalogue"\nsidebar: false\ntoc: false\n---\n\n'
            + "Browse datasets available through the lab's Goldmine. Select a dataset to see "
            + "its description, version, resources, and retrieval instructions.\n\n"
            + table
            + "\n\n## About this catalogue\n\n"
            + "Entries appear after publication and fresh-retrieval verification. "
            + "Data remain in Goldmine; this site presents metadata and retrieval instructions.\n\n"
            + f"{NOTICE}\n\n"
            + "See the [Operator Manual](overview.qmd) to register and publish a dataset.\n"
        )
        _write(config.website / "index.qmd", index)
        # Delete only files previously generated by Depot, never an uncontrolled scan.
        previous = read_json(config.state / "catalogue-pages.json") or {"pages": []}
        for relative in set(previous["pages"]) - set(pages):
            from .config import contained

            path = contained(config.website / relative, config.website / "datasets")
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        write_json(config.state / "catalogue-pages.json", {"pages": pages})
        return (
            data.loc[:, ["id", "version"]]
            .rename(columns={"id": "dataset_id"})
            .assign(status="catalogued")
            .to_dict(orient="records")
        )

title: Command-line interface
text:
For a new dataset, follow the README setup and real-data walkthrough. Register the completed release first, then run fetch ID VERSION, validate ID VERSION, and push ID VERSION, in that order, with the same --config FILE on every command. Validation does not fetch implicitly. After a verified push, run catalog build with that configuration and render its website with scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring. The catalogue and Manual share notebooks/ and render to docs/. Inspect errors with receipts ID.
sync automates these steps through catalogue generation for every dataset and release directory in the selected registry; it has no dataset selector and does not render the website. Use individual commands for a selected release.
Interactive commands show the active phase and elapsed time. Fingerprinting reports file counts. Validation runs resources in parallel by default and reports its phase; set PYTHON_CPU_COUNT before launching Depot to limit workers. Packages with foreign keys run sequentially, identifying each resource and reporting rows every 10,000 rows. Those row counts restart for each resource and do not imply a known total or an estimated completion time. Redirected output and batch jobs receive plain status lines on stderr, with repeated counts limited to one line per 30 seconds. --json suppresses all progress and keeps stdout machine-readable; receipts also remain JSON-only. Ctrl-C stops the display and returns exit status 130.

title: Command-line interface
text:
Run manual and batch operations

cli.py






Tip Procedure



"""Small Rich/argparse interface over the release lifecycle."""

import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from time import monotonic

from rich.console import Console
from rich.progress import Progress, SpinnerColumn, TextColumn, TimeElapsedColumn
from rich.table import Table
from rich.text import Text

from .catalog import build
from .config import Config
from .errors import DepotError
from .progress import ProgressUpdate, quiet
from .service import Depot


class CLIProgress:
    """Render live Rich status in terminals and bounded status logs in batch jobs."""

    def __init__(self, enabled: bool = True, console: Console | None = None):
        self.enabled = enabled
        self.console = console if console is not None else Console(stderr=True)
        self.display = Progress(
            SpinnerColumn(),
            TextColumn("{task.description}", markup=False),
            TextColumn("{task.fields[count]}", markup=False),
            TimeElapsedColumn(),
            console=self.console,
            transient=True,
            disable=not enabled or not self.console.is_terminal,
        )
        self.task = self.display.add_task("Starting Depot", total=None, count="")
        self.started = monotonic()
        self.last_message = None
        self.last_logged = self.started

    def start(self) -> None:
        self.display.start()

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self.display.stop()

    def __call__(self, update: ProgressUpdate) -> None:
        if not self.enabled:
            return
        count = ""
        if update.completed is not None:
            count = f"{update.completed:,}"
            if update.total is not None:
                count += f"/{update.total:,}"
            count += f" {update.unit}"
        self.display.update(self.task, description=update.message, count=count)
        if not self.console.is_terminal:
            now = monotonic()
            if update.message != self.last_message or now - self.last_logged >= 30:
                suffix = f" — {count}" if count else ""
                self.console.print(Text(f"[{now - self.started:,.1f}s] {update.message}{suffix}"))
                self.last_logged = now
        self.last_message = update.message


def parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    result = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Validate and publish immutable Prospector releases."
    )
    result.add_argument(
        "--config", type=Path, default=Path(os.environ.get("DEPOT_CONFIG", "depot.toml"))
    )
    result.add_argument(
        "--json", action="store_true", help="Emit JSON results only, without progress messages."
    )
    commands = result.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name in ("fetch", "validate", "push"):
        command = commands.add_parser(name)
        command.add_argument("dataset_id")
        command.add_argument("version")
    commands.add_parser("sync")
    catalogue = commands.add_parser("catalog")
    catalogue.add_argument("action", choices=["build"])
    receipts = commands.add_parser(
        "receipts", help="Inspect internal attempt history, including rejected releases."
    )
    receipts.add_argument("dataset_id")
    return result


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parser().parse_args(argv)
    progress = CLIProgress(enabled=not args.json and args.command != "receipts")
    progress.start()
    on_progress = progress if progress.enabled else quiet
    interrupted = False
    try:
        on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Loading Depot configuration"))
        config = Config.load(args.config)
        depot = Depot(config, on_progress=on_progress)
        if args.command == "catalog":
            on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Building catalogue from verified publication receipts"))
            results = build(config)
        elif args.command == "receipts":
            results = depot.receipts(args.dataset_id)
        elif args.command == "sync":
            results = depot.sync()
            # Even when one dataset fails, catalogue prior and other successful releases.
            on_progress(ProgressUpdate("Building catalogue from verified publication receipts"))
            build(config)
        else:
            results = [getattr(depot, args.command)(args.dataset_id, args.version)]
        failed = (
            any(row.get("status") == "failed" for row in results)
            if args.command != "receipts"
            else False
        )
    except DepotError as exc:
        results = [{
            "dataset_id": getattr(args, "dataset_id", None),
            "version": getattr(args, "version", None),
            "status": "failed",
            "error": exc.as_dict(),
        }]
        failed = True
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        results = [{
            "dataset_id": getattr(args, "dataset_id", None),
            "version": getattr(args, "version", None),
            "status": "interrupted",
            "error": DepotError("interrupted", "Operation interrupted.").as_dict(),
        }]
        failed = interrupted = True
    finally:
        progress.stop()
    if args.json or args.command == "receipts":
        print(json.dumps(results, sort_keys=True, indent=2))
    else:
        table = Table("Dataset", "Version", "Status", "Detail")
        for result in results:
            table.add_row(
                result.get("dataset_id") or "—",
                result.get("version") or "—",
                result.get("status", "—"),
                (result.get("error") or {}).get("message", ""),
            )
        Console().print(table)
    return 130 if interrupted else (1 if failed else 0)

title: Operate Depot
text:
Depot consumes completed Prospector releases, validates and publishes them with DataLad, and generates a data catalogue from verified publication receipts. By default, verified releases are also available as ordinary writable files at GOLDMINE/LAYER/ID.data/releases/VERSION/; lab members can use them without DataLad. The RIA archive retains versioned history. This Manual explains the workflow and emits the depot Python library.
The site uses the shared Quarto Manuals format under notebooks/, an authoring profile for reading, an explicit emit profile for synchronizing generated files, and isolated rendering. The emitted application is a Python library rather than an R targets pipeline. Neither profile executes data processing or publication.

title: Operate Depot
text:
Set up Depot
Run from the repository root with the installed Spack environment available:
spack env activate -d .
export UV_PYTHON="$PWD/.spack-env/view/bin/python"
uv sync --locked
Git with an author identity, DataLad, git-annex, and Quarto 1.9+ must be on PATH. Select a reviewed depot.toml with registry, source, state, staging, workspace, public site sources, and approved publication roots. Relative configuration paths resolve from that file’s directory. Operational and website roots must be disjoint.
For this checkout’s configuration:
export DEPOT_CONFIG="$PWD/depot.toml"
Set website = "notebooks" in the configuration. The existing notebooks/_quarto.yml controls the catalogue and Manual together and renders both to docs/. The root README supplies the complete configuration examples. See configuration for the validated contract.

title: Operate Depot
text:
Add data to the catalogue
Start with a completed release containing VERSION/datapackage.json and every declared local resource. Add a reviewed registry/ID.yaml entry pointing to the directory containing the release versions, with a matching approved target and catalogue.visible: true. Relative source paths resolve from the registry directory. Registry entries do not fetch or publish data themselves.
For kiribati-biomarkers version v0.2.2, run each command only after the previous command succeeds, using the same configuration throughout:
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" fetch kiribati-biomarkers v0.2.2
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" validate kiribati-biomarkers v0.2.2
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" push kiribati-biomarkers v0.2.2
uv run --locked depot --config "$DEPOT_CONFIG" catalog build
scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring
Expect fetched, validated, success, and catalogued. Validation requires an existing fetched snapshot. Publication is successful only after a fresh clone retrieves and validates the published release. Open the rendered catalogue at docs/index.html. Supporting pages explain how to operate Depot.
The operator guide explains the sequence; the catalogue guide shows the pandas DataFrames and Great Tables used to present verified releases. There is no page template engine or separate list of catalogue entries to maintain. sync automates the pipeline for every registered dataset; use the individual commands for one selected release.

Render documentation or synchronize generated files






Tip Procedure



scripts/render-isolated --profile authoring

Run depot --config CONFIG catalog build before rendering to refresh public metadata from verified receipts. Rendering itself uses that saved snapshot and does not open private operational state. notebooks/index.qmd and the generated datasets/ pages belong to catalogue generation; authored Manual pages such as overview.qmd are preserved.
The default authoring profile renders the site and sets QUARTO_EMIT=0. The helper clears any inherited QUARTO_EMIT before Quarto loads the selected profile, because existing shell variables take precedence over profile environment files. The explicit emit profile sets QUARTO_EMIT=1 and synchronizes generated files from the reviewed procedure blocks. Both use the shared GoldenPlanetaryHealthLab/quarto-manual-html format with computation disabled.
The helper stages only public catalogue snapshots, Manual, and software sources. It excludes Quarto caches, rendered sidecars, and notebook checkpoints; operational configuration, registry, data, state, staging, workspace, and publication storage are never staged. Files and documentation are promoted only after Quarto finishes successfully.

title: Render and emit the Manual
text:
Isolated render helper






Tip Procedure



#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

script_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
project_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "${script_dir}/.." && pwd)
stage_dir=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/depot-manual.XXXXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf -- "$stage_dir"' EXIT
stage_project="$stage_dir/project"

export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$stage_dir/xdg-cache"
export XDG_DATA_HOME="$stage_dir/xdg-data"
export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$stage_dir/xdg-runtime"
mkdir -p "$stage_project" "$XDG_CACHE_HOME" "$XDG_DATA_HOME" "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR"

# Copy only documentation and software, never operational data or configuration.
for directory in notebooks src scripts examples tests; do
  rsync -a \
    --exclude '.quarto' \
    --exclude 'site_libs' \
    --exclude '*_files' \
    --exclude '*.html' \
    --exclude '.ipynb_checkpoints' \
    --exclude '__pycache__' \
    "$project_dir/$directory" "$stage_project/"
done
cp "$project_dir/README.md" "$stage_project/README.md"

(
  cd "$stage_project"
  # Quarto profile environment files do not override inherited shell variables.
  unset QUARTO_EMIT
  quarto render notebooks "$@"
)

emit_manifest="$stage_project/notebooks/.quarto/quarto-emit-manifest.tsv"
if [[ -f "$emit_manifest" ]]; then
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r emitted_path source_page; do
    [[ -n "$emitted_path" && -n "$source_page" ]] || continue
    source_file=$(realpath -e "$stage_project/notebooks/$source_page")
    case "$source_file" in
      "$stage_project"/notebooks/*.qmd) ;;
      *) echo "Refusing emit source outside notebooks: $source_page" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    staged_file=$(realpath -e "$stage_project/notebooks/$emitted_path")
    case "$staged_file" in
      "$stage_project"/src/depot/*|"$stage_project"/scripts/render-isolated) ;;
      *) echo "Refusing unexpected emit target: $staged_file" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    destination="$project_dir/${staged_file#"$stage_project"/}"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
    # Generated headers use source basenames, so no temporary paths need rebasing.
    rsync -a "$staged_file" "$destination"
  done < "$emit_manifest"
fi

rsync -a --delete "$stage_project/docs/" "$project_dir/docs/"
